title: Three-Week Yellow
cues: Main and Peach. One light. Stuck on yellow since the storm.
Neon yellow glow spills onto Main Street, a single streetlight casting long shadows
intro_or_break
County said Tuesday. That was three Tuesdays ago.
Dust motes dance in a shaft of sunlight illuminating a weathered calendar
intro_or_break
Whole town treats it like a handshake now
A blurred crowd of silhouettes wave, a rhythmic hand gesture in the heat
intro_or_break
You roll up, you wave, you go, nobody floors it, nobody freezes
Slow-motion figures stroll down Main Street, a relaxed and unhurried movement
intro_or_break
Mrs. Delgado waves with her coffee and a donut in her teeth
A woman's silhouette waves, a coffee cup and a glazed donut visible in the light
drive
Kids on bikes salute like it is a flag they invented
Children’s silhouettes ride bicycles, a respectful salute in the fading sun
drive
Pastor says it is a metaphor. Uncle Ray says it is a lawsuit waiting
A dark figure stands beside a weathered bench, a concerned expression in the distance
drive
I say it is the first thing this town agreed on since the water tower color fight
A rusty water tower stands in the distance, a faded blue-grey against the yellow light
drive
Sheriff sits in the lot with a sandwich and watches us practice patience
A lone sheriff figure sits in a pickup truck, a sandwich and watchful eyes
drive
He ticketed exactly one person. Tourist from out of county who honked. We clapped
Hands clap in unison, a wave of rhythmic motion in the afternoon sun
drive
Hardware store put a tip jar by the register labeled light fund
A glass jar filled with folded bills and hopeful gestures sits patiently on the counter
drive
It is full of IOUs and one actual twenty from somebody feeling guilty
Dry-erase marker streaks across a countdown, a child's playful interaction fading quickly
drive
Barber shop window has a countdown in dry-erase that nobody updates
The darkened window of a barbershop holds the ghost of a disappearing number
drive
Day fourteen got erased by a kid's forehead. We left the smear. History.
A smear of dry erase marker remains on the glass, an ambiguous historical marker
drive
Three-week yellow, wave and go
Silhouettes wave in slow motion, a rhythmic and hopeful movement
drive
Main and Peach moving slow
A single streetlight illuminates the intersection, a gentle, persistent glow
drive
Caution means we figured it out
Figures pause, contemplating a painted sign, a shared understanding slowly forming
drive
Ain't a law, just a local vow
Hands reach out, a quiet agreement in the warm, hazy light
drive
Three-week yellow, hold the line
Silhouettes hold steadfast, a commitment etched in the summer air
drive
Small town making its own green light
The intersection glows softly, a small town's unique and enduring rhythm
drive
High school painted a mural on the plywood by the hardware store
Plywood wall, faded mural of a sun, hardware store silhouette, warm amber light
drive
A giant yellow circle that says WE GOT THIS in letterman font
Giant yellow circle glows, letterman font, blurred figures admiring it, hazy gold
drive
Bake sale moved under the light so the cookies could bless the traffic
Small bake sale tables beneath a single spotlight, golden cookies, traffic stream fades
drive
I bought three and got stuck behind a tractor for a full hymn length
A slow-moving tractor dominates a dusty road, a long shadow stretches out
drive
Somebody started a pool on which day the county truck shows up
Crowd of hands holding betting slips, a weathered bulletin board in the background
drive
I put five on never. Ray put ten on Friday. Friday came. Ray ate his hat. Literally. Straw brim. We have photos
A man devouring a straw hat, bright yellow, blurred figures watching in disbelief
drive
Mayor gave a speech about community spirit then ran the yellow without waving
Mayor stands awkwardly before a floodlight, a receding crowd of indistinct figures
drive
We parked a cone in his driveway. Friendly cone. Message received
A friendly, upright cone sits in a driveway, a peaceful suburban street backdrop
drive
Football team started jogging in place at the light for luck before away games
Football players in motion, jogging in place, a streetlight illuminates them
drive
They went three and one. Coincidence. Still sacred now
Empty football field, golden light, a sense of quiet victory, faded cheers
drive
Gas station started giving free coffee to anyone who waved first
Gas station pumps glow warmly, a hand raises in a gesture of greeting, steam rises
drive
Owner said it was marketing. We said it was theology with caffeine
A weathered owner stares intently at the light, dark amplifier room tone persists
drive
Day twenty-two. Bucket truck.
A towering bucket truck dominates the skyline, a single spotlight shines down
drive
Guy in a hard hat looks at the light like it offended his mother.
Hard-hatted worker stares intensely at the streetlight, a feeling of unease
drive
Whole sidewalk goes quiet.
The sidewalk stills, a muted, expectant stillness, a distant streetlight glows
drive
He flips a switch. Green. Red. Normal again.
A switch flickers, green and red lights pulse, returning to normal, blurred motion
drive
First car hesitates like it forgot the alphabet
A vintage car hesitates at a stoplight, reflection in the chrome, stillness
drive
Mrs. Delgado waves anyway. Habit. Holy habit
Mrs. Delgado waves with a comforting, familiar gesture, a warmly lit street
drive
I miss the yellow already. Damn. That is a sentence I never thought I would say
A lone, yellow streetlamp, a feeling of wistful longing, faded colors
drive
County sent a survey. How was your wait. I wrote: we were fine. You were late.
A stack of surveys sits on a picnic table, a hazy, rural landscape behind
drive
Driver ed teacher kept using the light as a pop quiz. Wave equals pass.
A single, bright spotlight illuminates a classroom desk, a hand raises
drive
Half the juniors graduated polite. That is a metric the state does not track.
Rows of silent, grey-clad figures in a high school hallway fade into mist

Silhouetted figure waves from a dusty highway, a peach tree glows
drive
Old habits. Good ones.
Blurred hands gently clap, reflecting in a polished wooden floor

Someone mailed the county a postcard of the mural.
A faded, oversized mural shimmers in hazy distance, a yellow circle
